title: Large Language Models as Psychological Simulators: A Methodological Guide

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing literature on the overrepresentation of WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, Democratic) populations in training data and evaluating cross-cultural simulation accuracy using specific persona prompts.
Synthesizing findings from prior studies showing that Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) systematically shifts model outputs toward more liberal perspectives.
Reviewing research that measures simulation accuracy across different socioeconomic statuses, noting higher fidelity for higher-income and highly educated personas.
Analyzing prior studies that demonstrate LLMs portray racial minority groups as more homogeneous than White Americans and exhibit lower simulation accuracy for non-White personas.
Citing empirical evaluations that found ChatGPT achieves higher simulation accuracy for male personas compared to other genders.
Referencing studies that assess simulation performance across age demographics, finding better representational accuracy for older personas.

Discussing the ethical risks and representational harms of misportraying vulnerable populations, such as individuals with mental health conditions and trauma survivors, through stereotypical or flattened simulations.
